accuracy.evidence: Every record was checked against a named source and rounded with 'about': cheetah about 100 km/h in sprints (Smithsonian's National Zoo gives up to 70 mph; Sharp 1997 measured 29 m/s), racehorse 70.8 km/h (Guinness), Usain Bolt's 2009 peak about 44.7 km/h, elephants about 25 km/h (Hutchinson et al. 2003, Nature), peregrine stoop over 300 km/h (RSPB), blue whale largest animal known, up to about 30 m, NHM's Hope skeleton 25.2 m, giraffe up to about 5.5 m (San Diego Zoo), bee hummingbird 5-6 cm and under 2 g (Guinness), ostrich about 2.5 m. 'Biggest' is stated as heaviest, so longer sauropods do not make it wrong; the car is about 5 m, so 5 cars match 25 m.

misconceptions.evidence: Each step targets a documented child belief: big means fast (the elephant is the biggest racer and comes last), the cheetah is the fastest animal of all (the falcon dive beats it), the biggest animal ever was a dinosaur (the prediction offers 'A giant dinosaur'), heaviest means tallest (elephant versus giraffe on the tape), and book pictures are real size (bird cards are drawn the same size before the real-size row). The challenge feedback names the same five slips plus the meaning of '-est'.

lab_distinct.evidence: The lab is built around records, not one measure: a timed race whose positions come from each animal's speed, a dive-versus-run race over the same time, a car-by-car length count to a whale's tail, a draggable tape that has to stop within 0.35 m of each animal's head, and ordering same-size bird cards by real size. None of these mechanics (race by speed, tape drag, ordering cards) can be reused for another topic by changing labels; the gate measured it under 30% like every other flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner finds each record before the text states it: the race shows the cheetah reach the flag while the elephant is a quarter of the way, the dive shows the falcon travel about 3 times as far in the same time, five cars line up exactly to the whale's tail, the tape reads 5.5 m against 3.0 m and three grown-ups appear beside the giraffe, and the real-size row shows a 5 cm dot next to a 2.5 m ostrich. The done messages only confirm what was seen.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions, each with a tempting wrong option that the next action disproves: 'The elephant: it is the biggest' (it comes last in the race), 'Yes, nothing is faster' than a cheetah (the falcon dive wins), and 'A giant dinosaur' as the biggest animal ever (the blue whale fills 5 cars). The reveal line says which way the learner predicted.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Wrong answers get feedback for the slip behind them: 'Big does not mean fast...', 'The cheetah is the fastest on land. The peregrine falcon is faster still when it dives', 'No dinosaur was as heavy as a blue whale...', 'Heaviest is not tallest...', 'Book pictures are not real size...', 'Close, but not the record...', and the meaning of '-est' words. In the steps, picking the horse, the person or a too-high tape each gets its own message (for example '3.5 m: too high, above the elephant's head').

readability.evidence: Kid text uses short sentences and everyday words (fastest, tallest, as long as 5 cars, shorter than your thumb) and passes the kid readability limit in validate_lessons.py; numbers in km/h appear only as small labels and in the adult text. On-canvas prompts are one short line: 'Who will win? Tap Go', 'Tap the smallest bird'. Adult text names the key words and passes the adult limit.

no_filler.evidence: Every kid paragraph states a record and the comparison that makes it concrete, every adult paragraph gives either figures with sources, the common mistakes or what the lab does. The content gate found no filler phrases and the explanation is under 12% the same as any other lesson, including 1079 Dinosaur Sizes, which it does not repeat (no bus, no see-saw, no film raptor).

mobile.evidence: Checked iPhone-width (390 px) screenshots in light and dark for every step before and after Show me, and 1200 px desktop: lanes and animals stay inside the canvas, the falcon label is clamped so 'Peregrine falcon' is not cut off, the whale and 5 cars fit with the 'you' figure at the end, the giraffe, grown-ups and tapes do not overlap, the bird cards go 2 by 2 on phones, and the real-size row sits on a white card so dark birds stay visible in the dark theme.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a button twin whose name contains its visible text: Go! / Race!, one button per racer, Falcon / Cheetah and on land / of all, Add a car / Take a car away, Tape up / Tape down (labelled with the animal being measured), 1 / 3 / 10 grown-ups, and one button per bird. The canvas aria-label is updated after every action with the result in words, the challenge sets a summary of all five records, and the walk gate's axe run is clean in both themes.
